statement: For a block matrix P = [[A, B], [C, D]] with A and D square, the inverse can be expressed in terms of the Schur complements of A and D: P^{-1} = [[(A - B D^{-1} C)^{-1}, 0], [0, (D - C A^{-1} B)^{-1}]] · [[I, -B D^{-1}], [-C A^{-1}, I]]. The source states this identity directly and identifies its key sub-expressions (the Schur complements) but does not walk through the elimination arithmetic that produces it from P; what is restated below is the structure the source actually gives — the partition, the Schur complements, the assembled formula, and the invertibility-equivalence fact — not a from-scratch multiplication proof.

symbols.dimensions: n x n, n = n1 + n2

symbols.meaning: Schur complement of D in P
Schur complement of A in P

steps.text: Partition P conformally as [[A, B], [C, D]] with A and D square blocks; this is the partitioning the inversion formula is stated for.

Form the Schur complement of D in P, A - BD^{-1}C, and the Schur complement of A in P, D - CA^{-1}B; the source explicitly names the first of these ('recognizing that E^{-1} = A - BD^{-1}C (the Schur complement)') and uses the second by the same pattern with A and D exchanged. Forming these requires D and A, respectively, to be invertible.

Assemble P^{-1} as the product of a block-diagonal matrix holding the inverted Schur complements and a block unitriangular correction matrix: [[A,B],[C,D]]^{-1} = [[(A-BD^{-1}C)^{-1}, 0], [0, (D-CA^{-1}B)^{-1}]] · [[I, -BD^{-1}], [-CA^{-1}, I]], as given directly in the source.

By the Weinstein-Aronszajn identity (cited by the source but not itself restated from it), (A - BD^{-1}C) is invertible exactly when (D - CA^{-1}B) is invertible, so the block-diagonal factor is well-defined as soon as one Schur complement is nonsingular.

assumptions.breaks_when: D is singular, so BD^{-1}C and the Schur complement A - BD^{-1}C are undefined
A is singular, so CA^{-1}B and the Schur complement D - CA^{-1}B are undefined

assumptions.assumption: The Schur complements A - BD^{-1}C and D - CA^{-1}B are themselves invertible
assumptions.breaks_when: one Schur complement is singular, which by the Weinstein-Aronszajn identity forces the other to be singular too, making the block-diagonal factor non-invertible

failure_modes.signature: the assembled block-diagonal factor cannot be inverted even though A and D individually are invertible
failure_modes.cause: A - BD^{-1}C (equivalently D - CA^{-1}B) is singular

failure_modes.signature: BD^{-1}C or CA^{-1}B cannot be formed
failure_modes.cause: D or A, respectively, is singular, so the formula as stated does not apply
